texts.setting.renderer.help: How the picture is drawn. Eden's OpenGL renderer draws on your computer's graphics card. It is the only renderer, because a Switch's graphics cannot be drawn in software at a useful speed. A computer that cannot provide OpenGL 4.6 cannot run this core. The graphics card is outside the core and is different on every computer. What it draws is written back into the console's memory at the end of each frame, so a savestate contains the pictures.
texts.setting.console_mode.help: Whether the console is held in the hand or sits in its dock. Games ask which, and many draw at 1280x720 in the hand and at 1920x1080 docked, with other details to match. When docked, the picture is 1920x1080. It is part of the console, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.resolution.help: How many times the console's own resolution the graphics card draws at (Eden's Resolution setting). At 2x the picture in the hand is 2560x1440, and docked it is 3840x2160. Eden draws what it can at the larger size (most 3D scenes) and the rest as before. This is part of the console and not only of the picture. What the graphics card draws is written back into the console's memory reduced to the console's size, and those bytes differ from the ones a 1x frame leaves. A movie therefore needs the resolution it was made with. Above 1x every savestate also holds the pictures drawn at the larger size, so savestates are larger and saving one takes longer. Each step up asks more of the graphics card.
texts.setting.state_pictures.help: What a savestate keeps of the picture. 'exact': at the end of every frame, everything the graphics card drew is copied into the console's memory. A savestate loaded later (when going back in time, loading a branch or seeking in TAStudio) then shows exactly what was on screen. This is what making a movie needs, and it costs speed: tens of megabytes are read back from the graphics card on every frame. 'fast': nothing is copied, and the game runs several times faster. After a savestate is loaded the picture is black or out of date until the game has drawn again. That takes a frame or two for most of the picture, and longer for things the game drew once and kept (a minimap, a prepared shadow). The game itself runs the same either way, with the same inputs giving the same result, so a movie made with one choice plays back with the other.
texts.setting.rtc_start.help: The date the console's clock shows when the game starts, in seconds since 1970 (UTC). The default is 3 March 2017, the day the console was released. From then on the clock follows the emulated console's time and never your computer's. It is part of the console, because a game that reads the date can act on it. A movie needs the same value.
texts.firmware.prod_keys.help: The console's own keys, copied from your own Switch. A Switch game is encrypted and cannot be read without them. They are never stored in a project or a movie.
texts.firmware.title_keys.help: The keys of the games you own, copied from your console together with prod.keys. A game copied with its ticket (an .nsp from your own console) usually contains its key and does not need this file.
texts.firmware.system_software: System software (a zip of its .nca files)
texts.firmware.system_software.help: The Switch's system software, copied from your console, as a zip of its .nca files. It holds the system fonts, the time zones and the system archives that games read. Without it, or with keys older than it, Eden uses its own open replacements for those, and most games run.
texts.slot.game.help: The game, copied from your own console: an .nsp or an .xci file. A homebrew .nro runs too. The file is read in place and never copied into the project.
texts.slot.savedata.help: What the game has already saved, as Emulator > Export Save Data... wrote it: a .zip with <TITLE ID>/... inside. A save folder copied out of Eden or yuzu is accepted too, zipped with or without the folders above it (nand/user/save/0000000000000000/<user>/<TITLE ID>/). It is put into the console before the game starts.
texts.slot.content.help: The game's updates and downloadable content, copied from your own console: one .nsp file each. The game starts with the newest update given, and sees every DLC given as installed. The files are read in place and never copied into the project. A file that holds neither an update nor DLC is refused. The game's movie needs the same files: an update changes the game itself.
texts.error.no_game: No game is in the project.
texts.error.no_gl_bridge: Eden draws with OpenGL on the graphics card, and Chimera handed over no graphics card. The renderer setting is opengl-hw, and this computer may have no OpenGL context to give.
texts.error.bad_renderer: '%1' is not a renderer this core has.
texts.error.bad_console_mode: '%1' is not a console mode this core has.
texts.error.bad_resolution: '%1' is not an internal resolution this core has.
texts.error.gl_not_loaded: OpenGL on the graphics card could not be loaded.
texts.error.gl_too_old: The renderer did not start. Eden needs OpenGL 4.6, and this computer's graphics card gives %1.
texts.error.gl_no_version: The renderer did not start. Eden needs OpenGL 4.6, and this computer's graphics card gives no version of it.
texts.error.no_kept_memory: There is no memory to keep the larger pictures in.
texts.error.no_prod_keys: The console keys (prod.keys) are missing. A Switch game cannot be read without them.
texts.error.firmware_unreadable: The system software %1 cannot be read.
texts.error.firmware_no_nca: The system software %1 holds no .nca file.
texts.error.firmware_not_installed: The system software file %1 could not be installed.
texts.error.savedata_unreadable: The save data %1 cannot be read.
texts.error.savedata_empty: The save data %1 holds no file.
texts.error.savedata_not_installed: The save data file %1 could not be put into the console.
texts.error.content_unreadable: The update or DLC %1 cannot be read.
texts.error.not_content: %1 is not an update or DLC this core can read. It must be an .nsp file of a game's update or add-on content, and reading it needs the console keys.
texts.error.not_a_game: This file is not a game this core reads. It must be an .nsp, .xci, .nro, .nso or .nca file.
texts.error.game_not_loaded: The game did not load. Eden says: %1
texts.error.zip_cut_short: %1: the zip file is cut short.
texts.error.zip_entry_broken: %1: %2 in the zip file does not unpack.
texts.error.zip_entry_method: %1: %2 in the zip file is packed in a way this core does not read.
texts.error.zlib_failed: The zip file could not be unpacked, because zlib would not start.
